To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method to build three-dimensional implicit stratigraphic models from remote sensing data on a tetrahedral mesh and applied this method to a regional model of La Popa basin, NE Mexico.

(i) a 3-D model can be built from remote sensing data using tetrahedral meshes; (ii) the model building process is fully integrated, i.e., the user can edit the model on arbitrary cross-section, which is not the case for most other methods; (iii) the user can easily add additional data during the process; and (iv) the model is consistent with the available data and the user's interpretation

(1) a global workflow for 3D modeling of stratigraphy is developed, (2) a new approach to model the geometry of stratigraphic surfaces from remote sensing data is proposed and (3) the method is applied to a complex basin in Mexico.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a 3-D modeling method that integrates remote sensing data and other sources of information in a consistent manner.
the development of a global workflow to build 3-D geological models from remote sensing data.
the development of a 3D modeling tool that allows the user to build stratigraphic models from a combination of surface and subsurface information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method proposed is a good alternative to generate a 3-D model of a sedimentary basin from a variety of data sources, with the advantage of a fast and robust interpolation on a mesh.
this study provides a new method of 3-D stratigraphic modeling that is based primarily on remote-sensing images and digital elevation model (DEM) and that is based on a tetrahedral mesh.

the method presented in this paper is an effective and efficient tool to build 3-D geological models from remote sensing data and subsurface data, and to integrate expert interpretations and other available information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this method is a robust and efficient way to build a stratigraphic model of a complex basin from remote sensing data, while integrating additional information.
this new method provides a robust and efficient tool for 3-D modeling of complex geological structures.
the new approach provides an efficient way to integrate remote sensing data in 3-D stratigraphic modeling, with a minimum of user input.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed method provides a robust and efficient workflow for 3-D model construction from remote sensing data, and can be applied to any region where the stratigraphic architecture is controlled by geomorphologic features.
a global workflow based on tetrahedral meshes is a convenient and efficient way to build 3-D geological models from remote sensing data.
a global workflow for the integration of multiple types of data can be achieved by combining the use of a mesh-based interpolation scheme with interactive editing of cross-sections.
